turn1.explanation: The unit fires on clause- and sentence-boundary punctuation, chiefly commas and periods, in running prose. It is strongest on commas that separate list items or clauses, and in mid-sentence comma positions in narrative or expository text.
turn1.evidence: Almost every marked token is a comma or a period, with the peaks (10) on commas in lists or clause joins ("customer service," "Pakistan," "20 min,"), while periods usually score a bit lower (6–9). Activation is weaker on punctuation in drier or more fragmented text, such as numeric lists and short sentence ends (3–5).
